title: Protocols to Co-Culture Human Primary Lung Cells in the Simple-Flow Device
author: Iriondo, Koornneef, et al.
materials: Seeding hPBECs on inserts (as monocultures) at ALI

steps.title: Prepare instruments and reagents
steps.instruction: Obtain local ethics approval, autoclave all scissors, tweezers and scalpels, and gather 0.18 % Protease XIV, 1× DPBS, co‑culture coating, 15 mL Falcon tubes, 6‑well plates, 10 cm Petri dishes, and a cell‑culture hood.

steps.title: Coat plates for hPBEC isolation
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL co‑culture coating to each well of three 6‑well plates, incubate at 37 °C for 2 h, then wash once with DPBS before use.

steps.title: Prepare bronchus ring
steps.instruction: Remove connective tissue, blood and mucus from a human bronchus ring with sterile tweezers and scissors, keep the cartilaginous white tissue, cut the ring open, and place it in a coated 10 cm Petri dish.

steps.title: Digest bronchus with protease
steps.instruction: Incubate the opened ring in 0.18 % Protease XIV in DPBS at 37 °C for 2 h using a water bath, gently shaking every 20–30 min.

steps.title: Collect and wash digested tissue
steps.instruction: Transfer the ring to a new 10 cm dish with 10 mL DPBS, collect released tissue by centrifugation (300 g, 7 min), resuspend the pellet in complete KSFM + GA‑1000 (1:1000) – 36 mL for three 6‑well plates (2 mL per well).

steps.title: Plate hPBECs
steps.instruction: Remove coating from the three 6‑well plates, wash once with DPBS, distribute the cell suspension evenly across the plates, change to complete KSFM + GA‑1000 after 24–48 h to remove floating tissue, then change medium every other day until confluent (≈1 week).

steps.title: Trypsinize hPBECs
steps.instruction: Discard medium, wash once with DPBS (10 mL for 10 cm dish or 2 mL per well of a 6‑well plate), add 1× soft trypsin (2 mL per 10 cm dish or 1 mL per well), incubate at 37 °C for 12–15 min, quench with double volume of SBTI, collect cells in a 15 or 50 mL Falcon tube, centrifuge 400 g for 3 min.

steps.title: Coat inserts for ALI culture
steps.instruction: Coat the apical side of each insert membrane with co‑culture coating at 37 °C for at least 2 h (up to 24 h).

steps.title: Seed hPBECs on inserts
steps.instruction: After trypsinization, resuspend cells in 1 mL BEGM, count, wash inserts once with DPBS, seed at 1.0–1.5 × 10⁵ cells/cm², add BEGM + 1 nM EC‑23 to both apical and basolateral chambers, optionally add 5 µM RI to improve attachment.

steps.title: Establish air‑liquid interface (ALI)
steps.instruction: When cells are fully confluent (≈3–4 days submerged), remove apical medium, add BEGM + 50 nM EC‑23 to the basolateral chamber (1 mL for 12 mm inserts, 500 µL for 6.5 mm inserts), and keep inserts at ALI for 14 days to 1 month, changing medium 2–3 times per week.

steps.title: Prepare enzyme solutions for hMVEC isolation
steps.instruction: Make 1× collagenase I and dispase I solutions, then prepare a 1× working enzymatic solution on ice (≈5 mL per 0.5 g wet lung; e.g., for 1.5 g tissue add 43 µL collagenase I and 400 µL dispase to 15 mL DPBS + CaCl₂ + MgCl₂).

steps.title: Coat dish for hMVECs
steps.instruction: Add 2 mL hMVEC coating to a 6 cm dish, incubate at 37 °C for ≥2 h.

steps.title: Mince lung tissue
steps.instruction: Finely mince lung tissue in an Eppendorf tube with scissors for ≥5 min, wash repeatedly with DPBS until the suspension is clear of blood.

steps.title: Digest lung tissue
steps.instruction: Transfer minced tissue to a 50 mL tube containing the 1× working collagenase/dispase solution (use 0.5–1 mL of solution per transfer), incubate at 37 °C water bath for 45 min, shaking gently every 10–20 min.

steps.title: Mechanical disruption and filtration
steps.instruction: Pipette the digested tissue 15–20 times with a 5 mL pipette, then repeat with a cut P1000 tip on a 5 or 10 mL pipette; vortex 3 × 5 s; examine under a 2× objective, repeat digestion if few cells; quench with equal volume of complete DMEM; filter through a 100 µm strainer into a 50 mL tube, washing the strainer with 10 mL complete DMEM; centrifuge 300 g for 10 min, resuspend pellet in 10 mL complete DMEM, transfer to a 15 mL tube, centrifuge again 300 g for 10 min, resuspend in 1 mL MACS buffer on ice.

steps.title: CD31+ Dynabead magnetic isolation (first round)
steps.instruction: Mix CD31 Dynabeads, wash 5 µL beads in 1 mL MACS buffer, incubate with cell suspension 30 min at 4 °C with gentle rotation, place on magnetic rack (≈20–30 s), discard supernatant, wash bead‑bound cells 4× with 1 mL MACS buffer, then add 3 mL EGM‑2MV medium to the coated 6 cm dish, transfer bead‑cell suspension (total 4 mL) to the dish, incubate.

steps.title: Post‑bead culture and medium change
steps.instruction: After 48 h, slowly aspirate 1 mL per 4–5 s, add 4 mL fresh EGM‑2MV medium; monitor for endothelial colony formation over the next few days.

steps.title: Further CD31+ bead purifications
steps.instruction: Perform up to three additional CD31+ bead isolations (using 1, 3, or 6–8 × 10 cm dishes coated for ≥2 h at 37 °C). For the second/third isolation, optionally coat one well of a 6‑well plate for FACS purity check. After each isolation, discard medium, wash with DPBS, add 1 mL TE buffer, incubate ≥3 min to detach endothelial cells (MSC remain attached), collect detached cells with 2 mL 10 % FBS in DPBS, centrifuge 400 g for 3 min, resuspend in 1 mL MACS buffer, repeat bead isolation using 3–5 µL Dynabeads (incubate 20 min at 4 °C), then plate evenly into 10 cm dishes with 10 mL EGM‑2MV medium per dish. Verify purity by IF or FACS.

steps.title: Trypsinize hMVECs
steps.instruction: Discard medium, wash once with DPBS (10 mL for 10 cm dish or 2 mL per well of a 6‑well plate), add TE buffer (2 mL per 10 cm dish or 1 mL per well), incubate 37 °C for 3–5 min, quench with double volume of 10 % FBS in DPBS, collect cells, centrifuge 400 g for 3 min, resuspend in 1 mL complete EGM‑2MV medium, count, and plate on freshly coated inserts or plates.

steps.title: Isolate hLFs from lung tissue
steps.instruction: Place a lung piece in a 10 cm dish, remove abnormal areas, cut into ~0.3 cm² pieces, add 3–4 pieces per well of a 6‑well plate, let adhere in a humidified 37 °C incubator for 20 min, then gently add 1 mL complete DMEM + GA‑1000 (1:1000) per well, incubate undisturbed for ≥48 h, refresh medium (1 mL) every other day, after 1 week fibroblasts appear; continue culture for 2 weeks, then transfer tissues to a T‑25 flask with 10 mL complete DMEM + GA‑1000 (flask placed vertically), later split adherent fibroblasts into a new 6‑well plate with the same medium.

steps.title: Trypsinize hLFs
steps.instruction: Discard medium, wash once with DPBS (10 mL for 10 cm dish or 2 mL per well of a 6‑well plate), add TE buffer (2 mL per 10 cm dish or 1 mL per well), incubate 37 °C for 3–5 min, quench with double volume of complete DMEM, collect cells, centrifuge 400 g for 3 min, resuspend in 1 mL complete DMEM, count with Countess 3.

steps.title: Sterilize Simple‑Flow plates
steps.instruction: In a sterile cabinet, submerge each 3D‑printed Simple‑Flow plate in 70 % IPA (≈2 L total) for 5–10 s, remove excess IPA with paper towels, let air‑dry.

steps.title: Assemble tubing and connectors
steps.instruction: Cut ~20 cm extension tubing, connect it to the three‑stop tubing using male and female Luer‑lock connectors, attach female Luer‑lock connectors to the tubing ends, then screw these connectors into the 3D‑printed plate at a 45° angle, ensuring uniform tightening.

steps.title: Set up peristaltic pump
steps.instruction: Place the peristaltic pump on a metallic tray inside the cell‑culture hood, connect the three‑stop tubing to two cassette stops, affix cassettes to the pump, adjust the pressure lever (2–3 clicks) for proper flow, and cover the plate with a sterile 24‑well lid.

steps.title: Prime tubing with IPA
steps.instruction: Pump 70 % IPA through the system for ~5 min at a speed of 0.5–1.0 mL/min (≈320–650 µL/min), check for bubbles in the holes where Luer connectors attach, discard IPA by vacuum extraction or pipetting until no liquid remains.

steps.title: Rinse tubing with DPBS
steps.instruction: Repeat the priming steps using DPBS to remove residual IPA.

steps.title: Load co‑culture medium
steps.instruction: Add 8 mL of BEGM:EGM‑2MV (2:1) co‑culture medium containing 50 nM EC‑23 per channel, verify bubble‑free flow and pink coloration of Luer connectors.

steps.title: Insert cultures and start flow
steps.instruction: Set pump speed to 0.01 mL/min (≈4 µL/min), insert cell‑culture inserts with hPBEC/hMVEC/hLF co‑cultures using sterile tweezers, place the entire assembly (plate, tray, pump) into the incubator’s water‑bath tray.

steps.title: Check for leaks and seal
steps.instruction: After the plate warms, inspect for pink medium stains; if leaks appear, tighten Luer connectors, apply autoclaved high‑vacuum grease along the groove between plate and connector, replace paper towels, re‑assemble, and return to incubator.

steps.title: Run flow experiment
steps.instruction: Maintain pump speed at 0.01 mL/min, monitor the system for 14 days, ensuring continuous bubble‑free flow and sterile conditions.

description: Current animal and in vitro models inadequately recapitulate the human lung characteristics, leading to suboptimal predictive outcomes for potential respiratory treatments and patient-specific situations. To address this limitation, extensive efforts are directed towards refining in vitro models that more accurately mimic the human lung physiology, such as differentiated epithelial cultures assessed for barrier function and ciliary activity,1,2,3,4,5 and precision-cut lung slices (PCLS),6,7 organ-on-chip platforms and 3D airway cultures.8,9,10,11 Within this evolving landscape, our co- and tri-culture systems offer a platform to also study lung biology. Here, we provide a comprehensive protocol for establishing co-cultures of human primary bronchial epithelial cells (hPBECs) and human lung microvascular endothelial cells (hMVECs), and of three-dimensional tri-cultures comprising human lung fibroblasts (hLFs) embedded in collagen matrices, alongside hPBECs and hMVECs. In the described configuration, the hPBECs are air-exposed to develop a differentiated muco-ciliary epithelium, hLFs are embedded in a type-I collagen matrix mimicking the lung submucosa, and hMVECs are plated on the basolateral side of membranes to be exposed to flow medium. Finally, we elaborate on manufacturing, post-processing, and setting up steps for a 3D-printed, biocompatible flow cell culture plated – termed Simple-Flow – that allows the integration of commercial cell culture inserts containing the lung co-cultures, and medium flow in the basal chamber.12 Protocols for isolating and culturing of primary hPBECs, hMVECs and hLFs from human lung resection material are described at the end of the manuscript.
